title: Cu clusters immobilized on Cd-defective cadmium sulfide nano-rods towards photocatalytic CO2 reduction

nodes.label: Solar CO2-to-fuel conversion needs a catalyst that works on light alone, with no sacrificial agent
Metal clusters normally need protecting ligands, which then block the sites that would do the chemistry
Cation vacancies at a sulfide edge should trap bare metal clusters and hold them there without ligands
CdS nanorods as both the visible-light absorber and the vacancy-bearing support

attrs.reason: visible-light absorption and a Cd sublattice that can be stripped

nodes.label: Cu clusters as the co-catalyst, anchored with no ligand shell

attrs.role: electron sink and CO2 binding site

nodes.label: Protonate in HCl, then anneal with CuCl2 in a sulfur atmosphere so the clusters assemble in the vacancies

attrs.reason: sulfur atmosphere keeps the Cu from oxidising and lets Cu-S bonds form in place

nodes.label: Three samples compared: as-grown rods, vacancy-bearing rods, and vacancy-bearing rods carrying Cu
Ethylenediamine-assisted solvothermal growth of CdS nanorods
Protonate the rods in 0.5 M HCl for 12 h to weaken and strip surface Cd
Anneal at 600 C for 2 h in a sulfur atmosphere with CuCl2 added
Rods 100-300 nm long, sharpened at the edges after treatment
Cd vacancies line the edges of the nanorods
Cu clusters of 1.6-3.2 nm sit on those edge vacancies rather than anywhere on the rod
The clusters bond through Cu-S at 1.54 A with no Cu-Cu shell, leaving the Cu cationic between Cu(1+) and Cu(2+)
The Cu-S interface pulls electron density off the sulfide, and the resulting internal field drives photoelectrons onto the clusters
Cd and S core levels shift up in binding energy and the carrier lifetime lengthens from 1.00 to 1.14 ns
CO2 binds far more strongly at low coverage: isosteric heat 25.4 against 8.9 kJ/mol
The route runs through an activated CO2- intermediate: carbonates give way to formate and the formate is consumed to CO
CO yield of 38.3 umol/g in 5 h, an average 7.7 umol/g/h, with no sacrificial agent

attrs.condition: Xe lamp, CO2 + H2O, 25 mg catalyst, no sacrificial agent

nodes.label: Turnover number 94.4 at 81.1% CO selectivity, against 54.4 at 72.2% for the bare rods
Cd vacancies immobilise ligand-free Cu clusters that both bind and activate CO2 and drain the photoelectrons
All three samples stay hexagonal CdS; no Cu or copper sulfide phase appears
Cu K-edge shoulders at 8980.9, 8982.1 and 8986.4 eV mark metallic Cu, Cu(1+) and Cu(2+)
Cu-S bonding is reported to put the wavelet intensity maximum near 4.9 inverse angstrom
Spin-polarised DFT on a 38-atom Cu cluster at a vacancy on the defective CdS (100) surface
STEM shows a Cu(111) lattice at 0.22 nm while EXAFS finds no Cu-Cu shell, so the two readings pull against each other
Above ~0.075 mmol/g uptake the isosteric heat drops below that of bare CdS, so the binding advantage holds only at low coverage
SEM shows straight rods 100-300 nm long; HRTEM shows one rod with 0.36 nm (100) fringes and a ragged, marked edge

nodes.label: Isosteric heat starts at 25.4 kJ/mol for CuCR SCC against 8.9 for CR, then falls below it beyond ~0.075 mmol/g

attrs.image_note: read from F5h. CuCR SCC starts at ~25.4 kJ/mol at the lowest uptake against ~8.9 for CR, the two cross near 0.072 mmol/g, CuCR SCC bottoms out near 3.0 kJ/mol at 0.105 mmol/g and then climbs back through the CR curve at about 0.125, reaching ~11.5 at 0.145. CR falls only from 8.9 to a shallow minimum of ~4.3 and back to ~4.6. So the Cu catalyst is the weaker binder only over a middle window, not at every uptake above the crossing.

nodes.label: CO reaches 38.3, 19.6 and 17.5 umol/g at 5 h, i.e. average rates of 7.65, 3.9 and 3.5 umol/g/h

attrs.image_note: bar heights read from F3a and F3c; the same catalyst also gives the highest CH4 (2.23 against 1.88 and 1.62 umol/g), so the selectivity gain is modest

nodes.label: TON and CO selectivity are 94.4 and 81.1% for CuCR SCC against 54.4 and 72.2% for CR, 48.1 and 72.6% for CR-H

attrs.image_note: values printed on F3e; the selectivity axis spans only 0-100% so the 9-point gain is a small step on the plot

nodes.label: Across three 5 h cycles the CO yield falls 38.3, 36.5, 33.5 umol/g, a relative loss like the controls

attrs.image_note: endpoint values read from F3f; CR loses 19.6 to 17.5 and CR-H 17.5 to 14 over the same three cycles, so CuCR SCC is not more stable in relative terms

nodes.label: Under light the carbonate bands at 1310, 1380 and 1553 fade while the 1691 CO2- band and the formate bands grow

attrs.image_note: the dark traces at the bottom of F4a carry the strongest carbonate bands; the 3D waterfall F4d shows the same species rising and falling over 0-120 min

panel_conditions.condition: CO2 + H2O mixed gas, dark for 0-60 min then Xe lamp to 120 min

notes: Lost: the EPR photoactivation series F2f, the wavelet-transform panels F2c/F2d, the EDS maps F1g, the FFT F1f, the Cu 2p XPS F5c, the band-alignment schematic F5g, the DFT adsorption energies (supplementary) and the CH4 branch of the DRIFTS pathway. Three audits: the 0.22 nm Cu(111) lattice seen in STEM is hard to square with an EXAFS spectrum that shows no Cu-Cu shell (o3, o6, n26); the isosteric heat of the Cu-bearing catalyst crosses below that of bare CdS above ~0.075 mmol/g uptake, which the text does not mention (o9, n27); and over three cycles the Cu catalyst loses about as large a fraction of its yield as the controls do (o12). Also read off the panels but not stated: the Cu-bearing catalyst gives the highest CH4 yield as well as the highest CO, so the selectivity gain is small (o10), and the EXAFS first shell near 1.5 A is shared with the CuO reference, so it does not by itself pick out Cu-S (o6).

changes: n19 -> n20 rel causes -> supports. The turnover number and selectivity are computed from the same run as the CO yield; that is claim-to-claim reasoning, not physical causation in the material, which is the distinction v04 draws between causes and supports.
o13 image_note: 'the bottom of F3' corrected to 'the bottom of F4a'; the node reads F4a and F4d, and F3 is the photocatalysis figure.

o9 image_note extended: the CuCR SCC curve crosses back above CR at about 0.125 mmol/g and ends higher, so the n27 limitation applies to a middle window of coverage rather than to everything above 0.075 mmol/g. This makes the audit less sweeping, not stronger.

panel_checks.note: F1h holds the two intensity line profiles, the upper one boxed and annotated 0.36 nm (Line 1) and the lower boxed and annotated 0.22 nm (Line 2). Both spacings the node quotes are printed on the panel, and the 0.22 nm reading is a resolved periodic lattice, which is what makes the n26 anomaly against the EXAFS real rather than rhetorical.

F5h plots Qst against CO2 uptake for CR and CuCR SCC. CuCR SCC starts at ~25.4 kJ/mol against ~8.9 for CR, the curves cross near 0.072 mmol/g and CuCR SCC bottoms out near 3.0 at 0.105 - every number in the node. The one thing the node missed is that the curve climbs back above CR at ~0.125, which has been added.

F3e prints TON 48.1 (CR-H), 94.4 (CuCR SCC) and 54.4 (CR) on a left axis, with CO selectivity on a blue right axis at roughly 72, 81 and 72%. Matches the node, and its image_note is right that the 0-100% right axis makes the 9-point selectivity gain a small step.

review.audit_summary: Three audit nodes (n26, n27, o12) plus two text-silent readings kept in image_notes (the CH4 yield in o10, the shared CuO first shell in o6), which is the right budget. The grading is careful and mostly correct. n26 is the best of the eight papers in this batch: it names a genuine internal contradiction in the paper's own evidence - a resolved 0.22 nm Cu(111) lattice in STEM against an EXAFS spectrum with no Cu-Cu shell - and leaves it as a stated anomaly qualifying n13 rather than picking a side. o12 correctly reads relative rather than absolute decay, which is what makes it an audit at all. n27 was slightly overstated and is now bounded to the coverage window the panel actually shows. Nothing in this graph dresses a 'does not resolve' finding up as a contradiction: o2, o5, o8 and o12 all carry image_support=partial, which is where those judgements belong.
